justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: ACLS-guided resuscitation is evidence-based for arrest care, and provider-course participation is associated with improved patient outcomes (Lockey 2018), but for a rehab clinician it is an emergency-readiness competency rather than a primary driver of rehab outcomes.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Directly relevant in ICU, acute cardiac, and telemetry settings; minimal relevance to general outpatient PT.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: No billing or payer impact — purely an internal competency credential.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: A 1–2 day provider course with skills/written check — among the cheapest, fastest credentials available.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Frequently required or strongly preferred for ICU/acute-care and cardiac-rehab therapist roles — real hiring relevance in those settings.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Tied to safety and emergency response rather than the patient's perceived rehab experience.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: None — no consumer-facing or cash-pay value.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: None — does not affect billing or pricing.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Common and expected in acute settings, so it differentiates little.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Minimal — not an ownership or practice-building credential.
justifications.business.efficiency: Very cheap and fast to obtain; the cost/time burden is trivial.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Carries little academic weight — a baseline competency, not a scholarly credential.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Grounded in periodically updated AHA evidence-based guidelines, but confers no research training.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: A narrow instructor pathway exists, but it is not an academic career track.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Built on AHA/ILCOR consensus-on-science guidelines — strong process evidence, though provider-course-to-outcome links are mixed (skill-decay literature).
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Essentially never a faculty hiring criterion.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Trivial cost/time, so high efficiency-per-dollar even though academic payoff is small.
